_README: THE CANONICAL LIST OF MINI APP DISCOVERY ROUTES. One key per DESTINATION,
not one per category, because the founder runs tools/miniapp_funnel.py
before and after EACH submission and five announcement channels are five
separate events. A single shared 'tg-miniapp-channel' key would make the
3.9M-subscriber channel and the 9,671-subscriber one indistinguishable,
which is the measurement that decides whether reach or fit is what works.
THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH. Two deployed artefacts mirror it and
cannot read it at runtime: ALLOWED_SOURCES in cloudflare_worker_miniapp.js
gates the ?startapp= value, and _SOURCE_ALIASES in
relayshield_developer_signup.py maps the key to a banner. A key missing
from EITHER is silently downgraded -- the Worker falls back to the generic
'tg-miniapp' and the landing page logs 'unmatched:'. Both are attribution
that looks like it worked. test_miniapp_routes.py fails if the three
disagree.
REGISTER THE KEY BEFORE THE LINK SHIPS. FD-8 is four months of arrivals
from the canonical MCP directory logging unmatched: because a link went out
carrying a key nobody had registered.
Ranking is from miniapp_discovery_and_stripe_choice.md section 2 and is NOT
to be re-litigated. audience_note records where each number came from, and
a number with no source is not a number.

routes.audience_note: UNMEASURED -- nobody has counted the blog channel's subscribers. Ours, and the only surface whose audience chose us, which is why it ranks first despite being the smallest.
routes.why_first: One first impression is spent per channel. Spend the first one where a bad reception costs least and the feedback is honest.

routes.audience_note: Measured by tools/find_miniapp_channels.py. @twa_apps is the SAME channel, do not submit twice.
routes.why_first: The largest single first impression we will ever spend. It goes AFTER the blog channel and after at least one small channel, so the app has been opened by strangers before it is shown to 3.9M of them.

routes.audience_note: UNMEASURED as an audience, and that is the wrong unit for it. The site's own search bar reports 6,616 TMAs and 5,335 bots indexed, which measures the CATALOGUE and not its traffic. A standing listing is worth doing whatever the number turns out to be.
routes.why_first: SEPARATE FROM rank 4 ON PURPOSE. @findminiapp is a Telegram CHANNEL and this is the web directory; they are very probably the same operation, and they are still two destinations. A channel post is ONE impression with a lifetime of a day. A directory listing is a STANDING surface that keeps returning arrivals for as long as it is up. Sharing one key merges a broadcast with a permanent shelf and makes the delta uninterpretable, which is the tg-miniapp-channel defect this table was rebuilt to remove. It is the FIRST submission we actually make, ahead of its rank, because findmini.app/submit/ is a plain web form with no bot and no sign-in and their stated turnaround is under 24 hours -- the cheapest possible test of whether our listing copy survives a moderator. The rank column is priority; the running order is the sequence, and the two differ deliberately, exactly as @telegtapps runs before @trendingapps.
routes.submission_note: SUBMITTED 2026-09-14 via findmini.app/submit/, the plain web form. Their page answered 'Thanks for your submission! We'll review your app and add it to the catalog.' Stated turnaround is under 24 hours and corrections go to support@findmini.app. THE FIRST CATALOGUE SUBMISSION THIS PROGRAMME HAS COMPLETED -- four earlier rounds went at Telegram channels and bots and none of them reached a form. The web-front-door-first finding is what changed it.

routes.audience_note: UNMEASURED, and the wrong unit for a directory in any case. A standing listing is worth doing whatever the traffic turns out to be, which is why it is not gated on a number the way an announcement channel is.
routes.why_first: SECOND of the web front doors, after findmini.app. Its submission flow is DESCRIBED rather than inferred -- sign in with Telegram, submit an app card (official link, description, categories, screenshots, language), team review before publication -- which is why the 2026-09-14 Top 15 ranked it first. FindMini overtook it on the day by being better than described: a named form URL, a named turnaround and a published exclusion list. Described beats inferred, and a URL that loads beats both. Registered BEFORE submission, which is the whole point: an unregistered key is silently downgraded to the generic tg-miniapp at the Worker's edge and logs 'unmatched:' on the landing page. That is FD-8, four months of it.

routes.audience_note: UNMEASURED. ton.app is the TON ecosystem's own catalogue and the one destination where TON-only is the HEADLINE rather than a limitation. Its own Terms of Service state that developers may submit an application for listing and that acceptance is at their discretion -- read from the destination's own page, not from a blog about it.
routes.submission_note: SUBMITTED 2026-09-15 through ton.app's own developer form. Awaiting review. The screenshots had to be generated at exactly 900x1600 -- ton.app states that resolution and an iPhone screenshot is 1179x2556, the wrong size AND the wrong aspect ratio, which is why dragging one in was rejected. Nothing about email or drag-and-drop was involved.

routes.destination: tg.app, a Telegram apps and bots catalogue
routes.audience_note: UNMEASURED. Described as free to list with a quick review. UNVERIFIED from the container: tg.app is egress-blocked here, so that is a search summary rather than their own page, and the founder's first step is to read the header and footer for the submission route.
routes.submission_note: SUBMITTED AND APPROVED 2026-09-15, the same day, through tg.app's own Creator Studio web form. Listed as 'Scam Checker | RelayShield IDCheck', Mini App, category Tools. THE FIRST LISTING OF OURS THAT IS ACTUALLY LIVE ON A CATALOGUE rather than queued behind a review. THE TITLE IS DELIBERATELY NOT THE BRAND ALONE. tg.app's own guidance is that Telegram search favours titles matching what users type, and nobody types 'RelayShield' -- so the listing leads with the term and keeps the brand attached. This changes NOTHING in BotFather: the app title stays 'RelayShield IDCheck' and the short name stays 'idcheck', because a catalogue title and a Mini App title are different fields on different systems and renaming a live surface for a search benefit a listing already gives you is a write with no upside. Its Claim Listing search returned no existing RelayShield record, so this created the entry rather than duplicating one.

routes.audience_note: UNMEASURED as traffic, and the wrong unit again: it is a developer-audience list rather than a consumer catalogue, so an arrival from it is more likely to be a bot developer than a person checking an address. That makes it a poor volume bet and a good FIT bet, which is the audience the tg-miniapp-bottoken route already exists for.
routes.why_first: THE ONE TO DO FIRST, because it is the only route in this table that needs NO IMAGE UPLOAD. miniTelegram's form crashed the page on four separate icon files and discarded a filled form each time; an awesome-list entry is one line of Markdown in a pull request, submitted from a browser with no file picker anywhere in the flow. Its CONTRIBUTING.md was READ rather than assumed: one PR per suggestion, appended to the bottom of the relevant category, format '- [Resource](link) - Description.' The Products section already carries an entry in the t.me/<bot>/<app> form, so ours fits the house style rather than asking for an exception.
routes.submission_note: SUBMITTED 2026-09-14 as pull request #77 to telegram-mini-apps-dev/awesome-telegram-mini-apps, from nzdsf2-gif:patch-1 into main. One file, one addition, no deletions, commit Verified, GitHub reports Able to merge. The entry sits at the bottom of ## Products directly after Receipt AI Split, which is the position CONTRIBUTING.md asks for. DO NOT EXPECT A FAST MERGE: that repo had 45 open pull requests on the day this was filed, so open is not the same as responsive -- the CrewAI #6550 lesson. Check it occasionally rather than watching it; this session cannot subscribe to PR activity there because the repo is outside the session's owner scope and a cross-tier attach is refused.

routes.audience_note: UNMEASURED, and it is the bot's own audience, which is small. Ranked here because it is CHEAP, not because it reaches anyone -- ranking a surface by how it performs in general rather than how it performs for US is the error that put this at the top of the first draft.
routes.why_first: DO NOT SHIP. /setmenubutton REPLACES the existing button, and that button belongs to the TI monitoring product, which keeps the prominent control. Shipping it means adding the key first, which is the check firing correctly.

routes.destination: DappRadar, the dapp catalogue, TON and Telegram mini app sections
routes.audience_note: UNMEASURED. UNVERIFIED from the container, and the label is the point: every candidate host returns 000 here, including findmini.app and storebot.me, both of which have accepted a submission from us. 000 is a fact about this container's egress and says nothing about the destination, so it can neither confirm nor refute a route. TYPE-CHECK IT FIRST: open dappradar.com and find the submit route in the header or footer, and confirm it is a catalogue rather than a paid placement shelf.

The Check tab is TON-only by Telegram-terms design, and every other destination has to be told that as a limitation; here it is the headline. Same argument the TON catalogues row already makes, against a destination with a web front door, which is the only kind that has worked for us.

routes.why_first: RANKED LAST ON PURPOSE, and recorded as a different KIND of destination rather than a fifteenth catalogue. A directory listing is a standing shelf that keeps returning arrivals; a Product Hunt launch is ONE DAY, which makes it a channel post with a bigger audience. It is also the largest single first impression left unspent, so it goes after a listing has proved the copy, never before. Take the --snapshot baseline before it, never after.

routes.audience_note: UNMEASURED. UNVERIFIED from the container: tgboard.com is egress-blocked here, so everything known about it comes from the founder's own screenshot of tgboard.com/en/add, which is a primary source and is better evidence than any search summary. What that screenshot establishes: a plain web form at /en/add, an account already signed in, five Type tabs (Channels, Bots, Mini-apps, Groups, Stickers), a t.me link field with a Fetch button, a required Category dropdown, Name, an optional Tagline for the card view, and a required Description. A 'Promotion' nav item means it ALSO sells placement -- which does not make it an ad broker, because the free submission route is right there on the same page, but it is the @telegtapps shape to watch for. WEB FRONT DOOR, which is the kind that has worked: four of our five submissions went through one.
routes.submission_note: NEVER SUBMITTED. Checked 2026-09-20: 'tgboard' appears nowhere in this repository, in any .json, .md, .py or .js. FIVE LISTINGS ARE OFFERED AND WE HAVE THREE SURFACES: the Mini App, @relayshield_bot and t.me/RelayShield. Groups and Stickers are not ours and submitting to them would be inventing a surface. ONE KEY FOR ALL THREE, because the rule is one key per DESTINATION and tgboard is one destination; the funnel already separates what happens after the click (a ?startapp= check lands in the check stage, a ?start=SRC_ arrival lands in the BOT stage), so splitting the key would make the tgboard delta two numbers that have to be added back together. THE FETCH BUTTON IS THE HAZARD: a form that fetches a t.me URL to read its metadata may normalise it and drop the query string, which silently removes the attribution while the listing still looks correct.

loop_keys.what: The share card. Someone posts a scam link in a group, one member checks it and forwards the verdict.
loop_keys.why_not_a_route: It is not a submission we make, so there is no before-and-after to run. It is the compounding loop the routes are meant to start, and it is the number that says whether any of them mattered.
Reaches people who already have the bot. It is a convenience for existing users, not discovery, and counting it as a route would flatter the funnel.
Anything arriving here carried no route key or one the Worker refused. A RISING count here is a defect, not a channel: it means a published link is losing its attribution.

loop_keys.what: A bot DEVELOPER pasted their bot's handle into the Check tab and followed the link to the API landing page.
loop_keys.why_not_a_route: It is OUTBOUND, not an arrival: nothing is submitted anywhere, so there is no before-and-after to run. It is the flywheel number -- the only Mini App visitor whose own product has the problem our endpoints solve -- and counting it as a discovery route would credit a submission we never made.
